description:
Found by the fz-kdt.125 refutation (2026-09-01), PRE-EXISTING --
byte-identical at bd03d922e and 41906b046 (not the identity axis).
Two witnesses, probes in session scratchpad (refuter probes/):

(N1) send two closures to self, receive both, P.run(f,10) each:
interp 12 90 (correct); JIT 11 30; AOT 11 30. Same class via
spawn+send to a child. The mailbox-delivered closure is invoked ONCE
where the source says twice (f.(f.(x)) collapses to f.(x)? -- the
11/30 pattern = one application of each reducer).

(N2) send one closure, receive, dbg(f.(10)): interp 11; JIT prints
NOTHING exit 0; AOT prints NOTHING exit 0. Control send(1,7) works on
both doors -- it is the closure crossing the mailbox, not the mailbox.

Three-path parity law violated twice in the closures-x-mailbox
intersection. Triage together; suspect the message-transport path for
callable values (boxing seam at the send/receive boundary vs the
receive type widening past finite callable sets -- see the fz-kdt.125
refutation's receive.rs notes). Related family: fz-kdt.117 (closure
carriers), fz-kdt.99 (threaded-closure interp crash).

comments.text: fz-kdt.119 refutation bycatch (F5): every closure-in-a-MESSAGE probe crashes identically at base -- interp 'RefCell already borrowed'; a semantic.rs:1194 activation-key assertion with two distinct lambdas; JIT/AOT silently produce NO output. Same family as this ticket's two witnesses (the silent-no-output mode matches N2's signature); fold these probe shapes into the triage when picked up.

Fixed in 69ab26027 (worktree wt-kdt130-build, based on c2041041e).

MECHANISM (one root behind both witnesses):

A closure that crosses the mailbox arrives with no settled call target, and
none will ever arrive -- the sender's lambda identity does not travel with the
message as far as the analysis is concerned. `materialize_closure_call_edge`
(src/compiler2/jobs/artifact.rs) found no `CallSiteSummary` for that callsite
and applied the Kleene reading: no targets named => the call never happens =>
lower it as `CallReturnFlow::NoReturn` over the empty type.

`NoReturn` is honoured at the native door by `emit_native_no_return_call`
(src/compiler2/jobs/native.rs) as `Term::TailCall`. So the call was emitted, ran
correctly, and returned its result to the CALLER'S caller -- the `Deliver`
continuation on the instruction was dropped on the floor.

  N2 `receive do f -> dbg(f.(10)) end`: main tail-calls the wrapper, the wrapper
  returns 11 to main's caller, `dbg` is never reached. Prints nothing, exit 0.

  N1 `f.(f.(x))`: the inner (non-tail) call becomes the tail call, so `run`
  returns `f.(x)` and the outer application never happens. 11 and 30.

The interpreter honours the instruction's own `-> deliver eN` and so was right
on the identical backend program -- which is why the dump looked correct.

FIX: the callee's transport CARRIER decides whether the call happens, not its
target evidence. A `TransportCarrier::ValueRef` callee is a real callable value
the boxed-apply wrapper can invoke, so it lowers as the live public indirect
call it is (the branch for that already existed; `public_indirect_return_ty`
already accepted `Option<&CallSiteSummary>`). Only a callsite with neither a
callable carrier nor any evidence is the dead call and keeps `NoReturn`
(fz-f98.18 preserved, pinned by its own test).

EVIDENCE: red at base on all three doors, green after, for
fixtures2/behavior/mailbox_closure_invoke.fz (interp 11/21/31; JIT and AOT
printed NOTHING) and mailbox_closure_twice.fz (interp 12/90; JIT and AOT 11/30).
Both carry Elixir oracles. They are rendering goldens deliberately: a dropped
continuation cannot be caught by an in-language assertion, since an assertion
that never runs never fails. Unit tripwire
`materialize_closure_call_edge_calls_an_unnamed_callable_and_comes_back` is red
against the base implementation under the new tests.

GATES: lib 1573/0/5, cli 24/0, matrix 458/0/9 (+6 = 2 fixtures x 3 doors),
aot_variadic_open 1/0, clippy -D warnings clean, fmt clean, release clean.
Canonical backend dumps byte-identical vs base on all 460 other corpus
fixtures; the only two that move are the new ones. Corpus behaviour sweep
(1176 runs, interp+JIT, base vs fixed): the only real differences are the two
new fixtures -- the other 13 are PID text inside panic messages and differ
base-vs-base too. Both fixtures byte-identical in canon and output under the
reversed job schedule (`Agenda::pop` -> `pop_back`). 20x JIT + 20x AOT stress
each: zero variance.

CRASH TRIO TRIAGE (the fz-kdt.119 bycatch, honestly split):
- "JIT/AOT silently produce NO output" -- this root. FIXED.
- interp "RefCell already borrowed" -- SEPARATE root, still live, filed as
  fz-kdt.150. It is `deep_copy_strict_struct` holding `Heap::schemas.borrow()`
  across its recursion while a closure field takes `schemas.borrow_mut()`.
  Reproduces identically at base and after this fix; a closure in a LIST
  message is fine, only structs/tuples.
- semantic.rs:1194 activation-key assertion with two distinct lambdas -- NOT
  reproduced at c2041041e. Eight probe shapes tried (two lambdas with distinct
  captures, mixed arity, branch-selected lambdas, list-of-lambdas, tuple-tagged,
  two spawned workers, receive in a recursive loop); all agree across doors
  after the fix, and all but the tuple one agree at base too. Either it was
  closed by intervening work (fz-kdt.132 is the likely candidate) or it needs a
  shape I did not find. Not carried as an open claim here.

Also filed: fz-kdt.151 (P3) -- a `case`/`receive` arm body parses as a single
expression, so a multi-statement arm is a parse error. General to the parser,
not to receive; it forced the fixture shapes here.

Doc updated: .agent/docs/semantic-fixpoint.md now states the carrier rule and
why the distinction is load-bearing at the native door.
